step1_analysis.circuit_type: Differential Amplifier / Delay Cell with Cross-Coupled Load
step1_analysis.description: A gated differential amplifier stage with a partially cross-coupled PMOS load. The cross-coupled PMOS transistors provide negative resistance to cancel the positive resistance of the diode-connected PMOS transistors, yielding high gain. It is likely used as a delay cell or gain stage in an analog FIR filter.

paper_reference.title: A 3.2GHz-Sample-Rate 800MHz Bandwidth Highly Reconfigurable Analog FIR Filter in 45nm CMOS

power_consumption.description: DC power consumption when the cell is enabled.

sky130_expected.calculation: I = VDD / R_eq. With VCM=0.9V, transistors are in saturation/linear. Expected current ~1-5mA per stage.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Based on typical bias currents for high-speed differential stages in 130nm at 1.8V.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gm_in * (rds_p || rds_n) since gm_diode cancels gm_cross.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cross-coupled load significantly increases the output resistance, leading to moderate to high gain per stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = 1 / (2*pi*Rout*Cout). High Rout reduces BW, but small parasitic capacitance keeps it relatively high.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for 130nm node which is slower than 45nm, but the stage is designed for high speed.

delay.description: Propagation delay from input to output.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Required to support high-speed operation, though slower in 130nm compared to 45nm.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC gain, 3dB bandwidth, and transient delay of the differential stage.
